provenance.note: Systolic arrays (output, weight and input stationary; 4x4 and 8x8) and streaming datapaths (FIR filter, 3x3 convolution with line buffer, saturating dot-product engine). known_inefficiency and levers are annotations and are never shown to the LLM. Baselines are measured with Vivado (Dataset/apply_measurements.py).

designs.Problem:
4x4 output-stationary systolic array computing C = A x B for signed INT8 matrices, C[i][j] = sum over k = 0..255 of A[i][k]*B[k][j] (A is 4x256, B is 256x4, C is 4x4 with 32-bit signed results).

Interface and timing contract (the transformed design must keep it cycle-exact):
- Buffers: A is stored in a 256-word buffer, word k = {A[3][k], A[2][k], A[1][k], A[0][k]} (byte i = A[i][k]); B in a second 256-word buffer, word k = {B[k][3], B[k][2], B[k][1], B[k][0]} (byte j = B[k][j]). Words are written with (a_we, a_addr, a_data) and (b_we, b_addr, b_data); buffers are only written while no run is active.
- Run: a one-cycle pulse on 'start' while idle begins a run; 'start' is ignored while busy. 'done' goes low when the run starts and is high exactly 265 clock edges after the edge that sampled 'start' (that edge counts as the first); it stays high until the next accepted start or reset.
- Read-out: after 'done', present a result index c_addr = i*4+j (0..15); c_data (registered, signed 32 bit) shows C[i][j] one clock edge later. Results stay stable while c_addr is read.
- Reset: 'rst' is synchronous to clk, held for several cycles; it clears the control state and the accumulators.
- Port list, module name and the exact 'done' / 'c_data' timing must not change. Internal structure (modules, memories, PEs, pipeline registers, skew, read-out) may be changed freely as long as every output matches the reference in every clock cycle.
designs.Module header:
module sa_os_4x4 (
    input         clk,
    input         rst,
    input         a_we,
    input  [7:0]  a_addr,
    input  [31:0] a_data,
    input         b_we,
    input  [7:0]  b_addr,
    input  [31:0] b_data,
    input         start,
    output reg    done,
    input  [3:0]  c_addr,
    output reg [31:0] c_data
);
designs.latency_contract: done is high 265 clock edges after the edge that samples start (edge of start counted as 1); c_data = C[c_addr] valid one clock edge after c_addr is applied; start ignored while busy; results unchanged after done.
designs.known_inefficiency: Annotation (hidden from the LLM): the input skew (os_delay) and the PE a/b forwarding registers are plain registers that Vivado maps to FFs/SRLs; each PE keeps a 16-bit product register plus a 32-bit accumulator in fabric logic around a DSP that could absorb the multiply-add (DSP48E1 MREG/PREG, async reset on acc blocks absorption); measured: Vivado keeps the two 256x32 buffers in LUT RAM (352 LUTs as memory, 0 BRAM; message Synth 8-5584, timing-driven) although block RAM is free, and the read-out 16:1 mux costs LUTs; the zero gating of the stream could be replaced by a clock-enable or by a shorter accumulation window.

designs.Problem:
4x4 weight-stationary systolic array computing C = A x W for signed INT8 operands, C[m][j] = sum over k = 0..3 of A[m][k]*W[k][j] with m = 0..255 (A is 256x4, W is a 4x4 weight tile, C is 256x4 with 32-bit signed results).

Interface and timing contract (the transformed design must keep it cycle-exact):
- Buffers: A is stored in a 256-word buffer, word m = {A[m][3], A[m][2], A[m][1], A[m][0]} (byte k = A[m][k]), written with (a_we, a_addr, a_data). W is stored in a 4-word buffer, word k = {W[k][3], W[k][2], W[k][1], W[k][0]} (byte j = W[k][j]), written with (w_we, w_addr, w_data). Buffers are only written while no run is active.
- Run: a one-cycle pulse on 'start' while idle begins a run (weight load into the PEs, then streaming of the 256 rows); 'start' is ignored while busy. 'done' goes low when the run starts and is high exactly 269 clock edges after the edge that sampled 'start' (that edge counts as the first); it stays high until the next accepted start or reset. The run stores the 256x4 results in output memories.
- Read-out: after 'done', present c_addr = {j, m} (c_addr[9:8] = column j, c_addr[7:0] = row m); c_data (signed 32 bit) shows C[m][j] one clock edge later.
- Reset: 'rst' is synchronous to clk, held for several cycles.
- Port list, module name and the exact 'done' / 'c_data' timing must not change. Internal structure (modules, memories, PEs, skew, output storage, controller) may be changed freely as long as every output matches the reference in every clock cycle.

designs.Problem:
4x4 input-stationary systolic array computing C = A x B for signed INT8 operands, C[i][n] = sum over k = 0..3 of A[i][k]*B[k][n] with i = 0..3 and n = 0..255 (A is a 4x4 input tile, B is 4x256, C is 4x256 with 32-bit signed results).

Interface and timing contract (the transformed design must keep it cycle-exact):
- Buffers: B is stored in a 256-word buffer, word n = {B[3][n], B[2][n], B[1][n], B[0][n]} (byte k = B[k][n]), written with (b_we, b_addr, b_data). A is stored in a 4-word tile buffer, word i = {A[i][3], A[i][2], A[i][1], A[i][0]} (byte k = A[i][k]), written with (t_we, t_addr, t_data). Buffers are only written while no run is active.
- Run: a one-cycle pulse on 'start' while idle begins a run (tile load into the PEs, then streaming of the 256 columns of B); 'start' is ignored while busy. 'done' goes low when the run starts and is high exactly 269 clock edges after the edge that sampled 'start' (that edge counts as the first); it stays high until the next accepted start or reset. The run stores the 4x256 results in an output memory.
- Read-out: after 'done', present c_addr = {n, i} (c_addr[9:2] = column n, c_addr[1:0] = row i); c_data (signed 32 bit) shows C[i][n] one clock edge later.
- Reset: 'rst' is synchronous to clk, held for several cycles.
- Port list, module name and the exact 'done' / 'c_data' timing must not change. Internal structure (modules, memories, PEs, skew and de-skew, output storage, controller) may be changed freely as long as every output matches the reference in every clock cycle.

designs.Problem:
16-tap FIR filter on a stream of signed INT8 samples: y[n] = sum over k = 0..15 of c[k] * x[n-k], with fixed signed INT8 coefficients that are symmetric (c[k] = c[15-k]). x[n-k] is the k-th last ACCEPTED sample (a sample is accepted at a clock edge where x_valid is high); before 16 samples have been accepted the missing samples are zero. y_data is a signed 24-bit result.

Interface and timing contract (the transformed design must keep it cycle-exact):
- Input: x_valid and x_data (signed 8 bit) are sampled at every clock edge. The delay line shifts only when x_valid is high. Samples may arrive back to back or with gaps.
- Output: a sample accepted at clock edge t produces y_valid = 1 and the result on y_data right after edge t+5 (the edge that accepted the sample is t). y_valid is 0 in every other cycle. y_data only has to be correct in the cycles where y_valid is 1; in other cycles it is not compared.
- Reset: 'rst' is synchronous to clk, held for several cycles; it clears the delay line (the window starts with zeros) and the valid pipeline.
- Port list, module name, the y_valid timing and the value of y_data in valid cycles must not change. Internal structure (modules, registers, multipliers, adder tree, pipeline stages inside the datapath) may be changed freely as long as the outputs match the reference in every clock cycle in which the reference raises y_valid and y_valid itself matches in every cycle.
designs.Module header:
module fir16 (
    input         clk,
    input         rst,
    input         x_valid,
    input  [7:0]  x_data,
    output        y_valid,
    output [23:0] y_data
);
designs.latency_contract: y_valid and y_data appear right after clock edge t+5 for a sample accepted at edge t (x_valid high); y_valid is low in all other cycles; y_data checked only while y_valid is high; reset clears the window.
designs.known_inefficiency: Annotation (hidden from the LLM): 16 constant multipliers are built from LUTs and carry chains (0 DSP expected at the baseline); the symmetric coefficients allow a folded structure with 8 multipliers on pre-added samples (x[n-k] + x[n-15+k]) that also fits the DSP48E1 pre-adder; the adder tree could use the DSP cascade (transposed form) instead of fabric adders; the delay line has a synchronous reset and an enable on every register (control sets); the datapath widths (17/18/19 bit levels, 24 bit result) are wider than the 18 bits the result needs (sum of |c| * 128 < 2^17).

designs.Problem:
3x3 convolution of a pixel stream: unsigned 8-bit pixels arrive row by row, 64 pixels per row, one pixel per cycle at most (gaps are allowed). The kernel is a fixed signed INT8 3x3 matrix. For every pixel that completes a full 3x3 window (row >= 2 and column >= 2 of the frame) the design outputs y(r, c) = sum over dr, dc = 0..2 of kernel[dc*3 + dr] * pixel(r - dr, c - dc), a signed 20-bit value. Rows are 64 pixels wide; a frame starts after a reset and the row counter does not wrap, so any number of rows is supported.

Interface and timing contract (the transformed design must keep it cycle-exact):
- Input: in_valid and in_pixel are sampled at every clock edge; a pixel is accepted at an edge where in_valid is high. Pixels of a frame are accepted in row-major order.
- Output: a pixel accepted at clock edge t that completes a window produces out_valid = 1 and the result on out_data right after edge t+4. out_valid is 0 in every other cycle. out_data only has to be correct in the cycles where out_valid is 1.
- Reset: 'rst' is synchronous to clk, held for several cycles; it restarts the frame (column and row counters) and the valid pipeline. The line-buffer contents need not be cleared: they are always written before they are read.
- Port list, module name, the out_valid timing and the value of out_data in valid cycles must not change. Internal structure (modules, line buffer implementation, window registers, multipliers, adder tree, pipeline stages inside the datapath) may be changed freely as long as the outputs match the reference in every clock cycle in which the reference raises out_valid and out_valid itself matches in every cycle.
designs.Module header:
module conv3x3 (
    input         clk,
    input         rst,
    input         in_valid,
    input  [7:0]  in_pixel,
    output reg    out_valid,
    output [19:0] out_data
);
designs.latency_contract: out_valid and out_data appear right after clock edge t+4 for a pixel accepted at edge t that completes a 3x3 window; out_valid is low otherwise; out_data checked only while out_valid is high; reset restarts the frame.
designs.known_inefficiency: Annotation (hidden from the LLM): the line buffer is a 64x16 memory with an asynchronous read (read-before-write), which maps to distributed RAM; a registered read lets it map to a block RAM, and because the access pattern is a delay of exactly one row it is also a candidate for shift registers (SRL); the 9 constant multipliers are built from LUTs and carries (0 DSP expected at the baseline) and the column sums can use the DSP cascade; in_valid fans out to the line buffer write enable, the counters and the valid pipeline.

designs.Problem:
Saturating dot product engine: two vectors a and b of 32 signed INT8 elements are loaded into memories through a write port; on a start pulse the design computes result = saturate_12( (sum over k = 0..31 of a[k] * b[k] + 64) >>> 7 ), i.e. the exact sum is rounded to nearest by adding 64, shifted right arithmetically by 7 and clamped to the signed 12-bit range [-2048, 2047].

Interface and timing contract (the transformed design must keep it cycle-exact):
- Load: while w_we is high, w_data is written to address w_addr of vector a (w_sel = 0) or vector b (w_sel = 1). The vectors are loaded before start and are not written during a run.
- Start: a one-cycle pulse of 'start' while the design is idle begins a run; a start pulse while a run is in progress is ignored. The edge that samples the accepted start is the first edge of the run and drops 'done'.
- Result: 'done' is raised right after the 36th clock edge of the run (the start-sampling edge counts as the first) and stays high until the next accepted start; 'result' holds the result from that edge on and until the next run finishes. 'result' only has to be correct while done is high.
- Reset: 'rst' is synchronous to clk, held for several cycles; it clears the controller (done low, idle). Memory contents are not cleared.
- Port list, module name, the done timing and the result value must not change. Internal structure (modules, memories, multiplier and accumulator pipelining, saturation logic, controller) may be changed freely as long as 'done' matches the reference in every cycle and 'result' matches in every cycle where the reference raises done.
designs.Module header:
module sat_dot32 (
    input         clk,
    input         rst,
    input         w_we,
    input         w_sel,
    input  [4:0]  w_addr,
    input  [7:0]  w_data,
    input         start,
    output reg    done,
    output reg [11:0] result
);
designs.latency_contract: done raised right after the 36th clock edge of a run (start edge = first edge), low from the start edge until then; result valid while done is high; start while busy ignored.
designs.known_inefficiency: Annotation (hidden from the LLM): the 8x8 multiplier plus the 24-bit accumulator is a candidate for one DSP48E1 (product register absorbed as the pipeline register, accumulation in the post-adder); the accumulator is 24 bits wide but the sum of 32 INT8 products fits in 21 bits; the saturation compares are wide (25-bit) while only the top bits decide; the controller has a 6-bit counter plus a valid register that could share state; the two 32x8 memories are small enough for distributed RAM, and a single 32x16 memory with one read port would halve the read logic.

designs.Problem:
8x8 output-stationary systolic array computing C = A x B for signed INT8 matrices, C[i][j] = sum over k = 0..255 of A[i][k]*B[k][j] (A is 8x256, B is 256x8, C is 8x8 with 32-bit signed results). It has 64 processing elements.

Interface and timing contract (the transformed design must keep it cycle-exact):
- Buffers: A is stored in a 256-word buffer, word k = {A[7][k], ..., A[1][k], A[0][k]} (byte i = A[i][k]); B in a second 256-word buffer, word k = {B[k][7], ..., B[k][1], B[k][0]} (byte j = B[k][j]). Words are 64 bit wide and are written with (a_we, a_addr, a_data) and (b_we, b_addr, b_data); buffers are only written while no run is active.
- Run: a one-cycle pulse on 'start' while idle begins a run; 'start' is ignored while busy. 'done' goes low when the run starts and is high exactly 273 clock edges after the edge that sampled 'start' (that edge counts as the first); it stays high until the next accepted start or reset.
- Read-out: after 'done', present a result index c_addr = i*8+j (0..63); c_data (registered, signed 32 bit) shows C[i][j] one clock edge later. Results stay stable while c_addr is read.
- Reset: 'rst' is synchronous to clk, held for several cycles; it clears the control state and the accumulators.
- Port list, module name and the exact 'done' / 'c_data' timing must not change. Internal structure (modules, memories, PEs, pipeline registers, skew, read-out) may be changed freely as long as every output matches the reference in every clock cycle.

designs.latency_contract: done is high 273 clock edges after the edge that samples start (edge of start counted as 1); c_data = C[c_addr] valid one clock edge after c_addr is applied; start ignored while busy; results unchanged after done.
designs.known_inefficiency: Annotation (hidden from the LLM): scaled variant of design 1 (same structure, 64 PEs, 64-bit buffer words). The 64 multiply-accumulate PEs can each use a DSP48E1 (64 of the 240 DSPs of the part) when the asynchronous reset on the accumulator is removed; the skew delay lines (7 x 2 lines of up to 7 stages) are plain registers or SRLs; two 256x64 buffers are large enough that distributed RAM costs many LUTs, block RAM does not; the 64:1 read-out multiplexer is a significant LUT cost; the controller and the zero gating fan out to every PE column.
